# Unity 2022.3 for DeepSeek Harness

Drive a running **Unity 2022.3.62f3** Editor from the harness: read and edit the
scene, run Play mod

e, capture screenshots, read the console, build players, and
execute C# inside the Editor process —
all as ordinary agent tools.

Unlike editor integrations that only support Unity 6, this plugin ships its own
bridge. It works on

stock Unity 2022.3 with no extra packages, no network access,
and no domain reloads for `unity_eval`

tock Unity 2022.3 with no extra packages, no network access,
and no domain reloads for `unity_eval`.
## Requirements
| Unity Editor | **2022.3.62f3** (international build) is the reference version. The bridge only rep
orts the Editor version (`isRequiredUnityVersion`); other 2022.3 patches (2022.3.46f1 and 2022.3.62f

1c1 were tested) work the same way and are never blocked. |
| Harness | any DSH build that provides

the `tools` service |
| Platform | Windows (macOS/Linux editors are detected but untested) |
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The plugin row `unity-2022` is inserted by `cordis.patch.yml`; the tools appear
in the next turn. To
remove it again: `plugin_manager remove_bundle dsh-unity-2022`.

The plugin sits in the awesome-dsh-plugin
review queue, so once the entry lands you can also install

it from the DSH
plugin directory with one click.
## Using it on other projects

The plugin lives in the **profile** (one copy for the whole harness) while the bridge
package lives

in the **project** (one copy per project), so the same tools drive any
number of Unity projects:

1. **Give a project the bridge** — pick one:
- `unity_open { "projectPath": "D:\\Work\\OtherGame" }`

installs, launches and waits;
- `unity_install { "projectPath": "..." }` installs the package witho

plugin's `unity-package/` folder to `<project>/Packages/com.dsh.unity-bridge`.
`Packages/com.dsh.uni

ty-bridge` is an **embedded package**: once committed, every
teammate who opens that project gets a

bridge automatically, with no tool call.
2. **Route a request to the right Editor** (in order of pre

the calling agent's working directory inside a project — that project is chosen;
- only one Editor

running — it is used.
With several Editors alive and no `projectPath`, the call fails with
`ambiguou

s_editor` and lists the reachable projects.
3. **Project version**: `unity_open` picks the Hub insta

llation that matches the
project's `ProjectVersion.txt` (all three local 2022.3 builds are candidate

s) and
falls back to the closest 2022.3 build. A version that differs from the reference
build is re
ported, never enforced.
## Publishing to a plugin market

A market is just "one index JSON at some URL" plus "the installable packages that index
points at",

so publishing means publishing the package and hosting the index. Do one or
both paths.
### 1. Publish the package to npm

`unity-package/`, `

install_bundle <some .tgz>` verifies t

### 2a. Get listed in the community catalogue

The market UI (`dshmarket`) and its site read the curated list
awesome-dsh-plugin: open a PR
there t

hat adds one entry for this plugin. Their CI refreshes `plugins.json` daily and the
market plus DSH'

s Discover tab pick it up automatically (usually within a day). This is the
shortest path to "strang
ers can search for it".
### 2b. Host your own index (format 1)
`market/index.json` is a format-1 index, already validated against DSH's own parser:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Put that folder (`index.json` + `icon.svg`) on any HTTPS address — GitHub Pages, jsDelivr
(pairs wel

l with an npm-published catalog package), or your own domain — then add the
`index.json` URL under *

*Settings → Plugins → Discover → Index sources** in DSH. Anyone
running that DSH can then find and o
ne-click install it.
Display metadata an entry may carry (all optional; `en` is required, `zh` may be added):
| Field | Meaning |

| `title` / `description` | localized text, a string or `{ "en": ..., "zh": ... }` |
| `icon` | path

relative to `index.json`, an HTTPS URL, or a base64 `data:` URL of at most 32 KiB decoded |
| `meta

data.keywords` | free-form search keywords |
| `metadata.category` / `metadata.labels` | ids that mu

st first be declared in the index root's `metadata.categories` / `metadata.labels` |

## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

* The editor package starts a loopback TCP server on an ephemeral port after every
domain reload and

publishes a per-project discovery file (path hash, pid, port,
versions). The host re-reads that fil

e for each request, so Play mode, script
compilation and editor restarts are transparent — a request

that hits a closed
socket is retried once against the new port.
* One request per connection, one J

SON line each way. Commands run on the editor's
main thread; handlers that must not block it (`eval`

, `build`) run their own
threads and are joined back for the reply.
* `unity_eval` writes a tiny C#

program under `<project>/Temp/DSHUnityBridge/`,
compiles it with the editor's bundled Roslyn against

the editor and project
assemblies, loads the DLL and invokes it — so editor-facing code can use
`Un
ityEngine`/`UnityEditor` without touching `Assets/` or triggering a reload.

Screenshots render through a temporary camera positioned by the plugin. The editor's
own Scene view

camera is not used: its transform only follows the pivot during a
repaint, which yields stale framin
g in the same frame.
